module_title: British Economic and Administrative Policies - Basic Understanding
introduction: The primary objective of British rule in India was to exploit its resources to enrich Britain. To achieve this, they introduced new land revenue systems to maximize tax collection and systematically drained India's wealth to England.

core_concepts.title: Permanent Settlement (1793)
core_concepts.description: Introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha. It recognized 'Zamindars' as the owners of the land and fixed the revenue amount permanently. Zamindars kept 1/11th of the revenue and gave 10/11th to the British.

core_concepts.title: Ryotwari System (1820)
core_concepts.description: Introduced by Thomas Munro and Captain Read in Madras and Bombay Presidencies. The revenue settlement was made directly with the 'Ryots' (peasants). It covered the largest area of British India (51%).

core_concepts.title: Mahalwari System (1822)
core_concepts.description: Introduced by Holt Mackenzie in the North-Western Provinces, Central Provinces, and Punjab. The entire village or 'Mahal' was considered a single unit for revenue collection.

core_concepts.title: Drain of Wealth Theory
core_concepts.description: Proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, this theory explained how India's wealth and resources were systematically exported to Britain (as raw materials, salaries, pensions) with no adequate economic return to India.

important_entities.name: Lord Cornwallis
important_entities.significance: He is also known as the 'Father of Civil Services' in India.

important_entities.name: Thomas Munro
important_entities.significance: As the Governor of Madras, he established direct land rights for peasants but kept the tax rates extremely high.

important_entities.name: Dadabhai Naoroji
important_entities.significance: Exposed British economic exploitation in his famous book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume Permanent Settlement covered the most area. However, it only covered 19% of British India, whereas the Ryotwari system covered the largest area at 51%.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A simple way to map the land revenue systems to their respective British founders.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember who the tax was collected from in each system (Zamindar, Peasant, or Village).
The 'Sunset Law' is frequently asked in exams; remember that it is directly associated with the Permanent Settlement.
